To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ageing of mouse oocytes is associated with changes in cortical cytoplasm that may impair the fertilization process.
the cortical granules are not uniformly distributed in the oocyte cytoplasm, and they are internalized into the ooplasm in a high proportion of mature oocytes.
the cortical granules in the oocytes of old females are altered and this may contribute to the low fertilizability of the gametes from old females.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of ageing-induced changes in mouse oocytes and its relationship with the fertilization rate of these gametes.
the study of the cortical cytoplasma and cortical granules of matured and aged mouse eggs.
ageing-related modifications in the cortical cytoskeleton and CGs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ageing induces a progressive deterioration of the CGs.
ageing-induced changes in the mouse egg cortex are related to the low rates of fertilization and early development observed in old females.
the ageing of the mouse egg induces changes in the cortical cytoarchitecture and in the CGs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ageing-induced changes in CGs and cortical cytoplasm are responsible, at least in part, for the poor fertilization of old mouse oocytes.
the CGs in oocytes collected 20 h after their ovulation and those recovered from old females show several changes that may be associated with the ageing process.
CGs from young oocytes are well preserved in their original position and shape, while CGs from old oocytes are swollen and show a high degree of internalization in the egg cytosol.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ageing affects not only the oolemma but also the cortical cytoplam and CGs.
the cortical cytoplam and the CGs are altered during ageing, and these changes could be related to the low fertility of aged mouse eggs.
ageing induces changes in the cortical cytoskeleton and the CGs.
